paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: when you're boxed in with nowhere to go, the LORD is already working. Israel camped by the sea because God told them to, and He said ahead of time that Pharaoh would chase them (Exodus 14:2-4). So the dead end wasn't a sign God had lost track of them. Moses told the people, "The LORD will fight for you; you need only to be still." (Exodus 14:14)

Now watch this, because it's the part I love. The people were terrified, and I get it, I flinched at every drip in that old drawer. But the LORD told Moses, "Tell the Israelites to go forward" (Exodus 14:15), and then He opened a path through the sea. Being still doesn't mean doing nothing, friend. It means trusting that the One who fights for you is also the One who makes the way, and then taking the next step He gives.

And look where it ends up: a song. Moses and the Israelites sang, "The LORD is my strength and my song, and He has become my salvation." (Exodus 15:2) They remembered what God did, then looked ahead to how He would lead the people He redeemed with loving devotion (Exodus 15:13). So when your own sea is in front of you, baker, remember who saved Israel that day. Then keep walking, and save a little room for a tambourine.
